policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role are allowed to create new records in any table, including the Service table, because they have Full CRUD access across all tables.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

policies.description: Any request to create or update a record must validate that all fields marked as required are present. For add_new_service the fields name and owned_by are mandatory.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Each tool call must be a single validated operation; the add_new_service call must be performed alone without bundling other unvalidated actions.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: The system must not fabricate IDs or any other data; the service ID will be generated by the API and should be used as‑is.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: If a required field for the add_new_service request is missing, the assistant must state which field is required instead of guessing or prompting for more info.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: If any of the above rules (or any other policy) would be violated by calling add_new_service, the operation must be halted and the specific policy reason returned.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
